messages:
elaine: Quick sync — I posted the PRD draft for the "Redwood API: unified scoring + embed parity" work. Need focused review on acceptance criteria, perf budgets, and a short list of edge cases we must block on before launch. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/PRD-embed-score-draft :eyes:
mike: reading now. can we tighten the perf budget for rerank? current numbers feel optimistic for tail latencies. :thinking_face:
ranjit: putting numbers from bench runs: p95 120ms for small models, p95 260ms for 8k context on 1xA100. If we want <200ms p95 for default tier we'll need batching/cold-cache behavior documented.
sarah: flagged two customer asks in PRD comments — priority routing to cheaper models for non-SLO requests, and stronger mismatch handling for embeddings drift. Both could affect acceptance criteria.
elaine: agreed. propose we split acceptance gates: "must-have" (safety/accuracy/regression), "perf" (latency/cost), "scope" (routing/variants). We should be strict on must-have and perf for GA.
mike: +1. For perf gate: define SLOs and an experimental protocol. e.g., p50/p95 token latency, p99 catastrophic stalls, and cost/unit. I can add a reproducible perf harness.
ranjit: I'll add a cold-start test in harness. We should include a KV-cache warmup step in the acceptance script to avoid over-optimizing for warm caches only.
sarah: edge cases I want listed explicitly:
- empty / null messages
- extremely long context (100k tokens) -> graceful rejection
- non-utf8 bytes in prompt
- repeated near-duplicate queries for rerank (thundering herd)
- huge embedding vectors (unexpected shape)

elaine: perfect. Can you paste the exact failure modes we want (what 'graceful rejection' looks like)?
sarah: sure. rejection = 400 + structured JSON error with code.EXCEEDS_LIMIT and hint to use chunking; no internal trace exposed. Example payload:
```
{ "error": {"code":"EXCEEDS_LIMIT","message":"Context exceeds service limits (10000 tokens). Consider chunking or summarization."}}
```
mike: also need fallback behavior: if primary model is overloaded, route to compatible smaller model and include metadata: "runtime_fallback": true. That should be part of acceptance for routing.
elaine: routing fallback must preserve safety checks. We should add a test that simulates fallback and asserts no unsafe outputs. Who owns that?
ranjit: infra + safety can pair. I'll write the harness hook.
sarah: on embeddings parity: acceptance test = cosine distance within 2% of reference for top-10 neighbors on evaluation corpus. Document seed & eval set in PRD.
mike: adding a short smoke test block to PRD now. Example (to include in PRD):
```
# Smoke acceptance steps
1) 1000 chat requests @default sync rate
2) assert p95 < 200ms for small models, <350ms for long context tier
3) run 200 rerank batches, assert score stability (Spearman rho > 0.95 vs baseline)
4) run 100 embed queries, assert neighbor parity
```
elaine: nice. Two decisions we need in this thread: 1) hard perf gate numbers (we can accept tweaks after GA if we document fallbacks), 2) whether routing-to-cheaper-model is GA or experimental. I propose: perf gate = p95 < 250ms default, p95 < 400ms long-context; routing-to-cheaper-model = experimental (opt-in).
mike: ok on routing opt-in. I'll push perf harness and post results by EOD.
ranjit: I'll add cold-start and fallback safety hooks to the harness tomorrow.
sarah: I'll update the PRD acceptance section with explicit error payloads and the embed parity metric.
deploy-bot: Deployment notice: staging cluster will receive a canary on 2187654350 for this branch.
mike: noted — will watch. @elaine I left inline comments about throttling defaults.
elaine: thanks all. please update PRD before EOD, tag reviewers. We'll have a 30m sync tomorrow if numbers look shaky. :calendar:
